summary:
[  edit  ]
The Lookup  CHOP  outputs values from a lookup table. The first input (the Index  Channel ) is an index into the second input (the Lookup Table). Lookup outputs interpolated values from the lookup table.
Both the Index and Lookup Tables can contain any number of channels.
An Index sample with value 0 maps to the beginning (first sample) of the lookup table, and an index sample with value of 1 maps to the end (last sample) of the lookup table.
The output  CHOP  is the same length as the Index input. It is the same number of channels as the Lookup Table input, and has the same channel names as the Lookup Table input. The output is filled with the data extracted from the lookup tables. Indexes that fall between two lookup table samples are interpolated. The lookup table can be sampled outside its range.
NOTE: The  Extend Conditions  of the lookup table are used in this case where the index is less than 0 or greater than 1.
The sample rate of the output is the sample rate of the Index input.
The Lookup  CHOP  can be used to fetch values from a color lookup table, where a single index produces red, green and blue channels. It can also be used for rolloff or decay tables, where it specifies how much a parameter drops with distance.

parameters.label: Index Range
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: ⊞  - The Index Range maps the index channel's values to the lookup table's start and end and defaults to 0 and 1. The first parameter represents the start of the lookup table. When the index channel has this value, it will index the start of the lookup table. The second parameter represents the end of the lookup table and behaves in the same way.

parameters.label: Cyclic Range
parameters.name: cyclic
parameters.description: ⊞  - Adapts the range of the Lookup Table (2nd input) for cyclic or non-cyclic input indices. When using a cyclic input index (1st input), the lookup value for index 0.0 and 1.0 result in the same value. To avoid this, set Cyclic Range to Yes and the lookup will cycle smoothly.

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: auto
parameters.description: Checks the right extend condition of each channel (Assumes type cycle and mirror are cyclic lookups).

parameters.label: Yes
parameters.name: yes
parameters.description: For looking up a cyclic output (oscillator, beat driven output etc).

parameters.label: No
parameters.name: no
parameters.description: For looking up a single wave (slider mapping, etc).

parameters.label: Per Index  Channel
parameters.name: chanmatch
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how index channels are mapped to lookup Channel tables.

parameters.label: One Lookup Table  Channel
parameters.name: onetoone
parameters.description: The first index channel is matched to the full lookup table.

parameters.label: All Lookup Table Channels
parameters.name: onetomany
parameters.description: Each index channel is matched with every lookup table.

parameters.label: Match by
parameters.name: match
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how index channels are matched with a lookup channel in 'One Lookup Table  Channel ' mode.

parameters.label: Channel Number
parameters.name: index
parameters.description: An index channel is matched to a lookup table by its index within the clip. Lookup tables are cycled if there are few of them than index channels.

parameters.label: Channel Name
parameters.name: name
parameters.description: An index channel is matched to a lookup table by name. Unmatched index channels are left "as is".

parameters.label: Interpolate
parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: When on, the input can be interpolated between samples. When off, the nearest sample is used.

parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.name: left
parameters.description: ⊞  - The left extend conditions (before/after range) for the lookup output.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate

* **Normalize POP (POP de Normalización)** * **Función principal:** Re-escala los valores de posición XYZ (o cualquier otro atributo) a un **rango de 0 a 1**. * **Características clave:** * Puede convertir coordenadas cartesianas (XYZ) en **coordenadas polares o cilíndricas** (latitud, longitud, radio), también normalizadas a un rango de 0 a 1. * Ofrece opciones para **Bias** (sesgar los números hacia 0 o 1), aplicar una **función de curva de búsqueda** (`Lookup function`), un `Exponent` (potenciar valores) y **Re-range** (re-escalar a otro rango). * Permite asignar los valores normalizados a cualquier componente de un atributo float2, float3 o float4. * **Uso simple:** Útil para preparar datos para mapeo de texturas, shaders, o cualquier proceso que requiera valores dentro de un rango específico. Por ejemplo, para crear un mapa de calor donde los valores más bajos son 0 y los más altos son 1. * **Null POP (POP Nulo)** * *
